title: The Most Effective Way To Manage Students With ADHD
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Responding to years of reader requests, Linsin previews his thinking on managing students with ADHD while explaining that a full treatment will come later in a dedicated e-guide. In the meantime, he offers what he considers the single most important and effective strategy available now: becoming genuinely excellent at general classroom management, since a calm, distraction-free environment has the greatest impact on students struggling with restlessness, impulsivity, and attention issues. He argues this foundational step must come first, because no other strategy—including future recommendations for legitimately different students—will be effective until it's in place, and because a strong classroom environment makes it possible to accurately identify which students truly need additional support. He notes that many students currently labeled, pigeonholed, or even misdiagnosed due to poor classroom management will simply thrive once placed in a well-run classroom.
points: Excellent general classroom management is presented as the single most effective and necessary strategy for students with ADHD.
A calm, distraction-free environment has an outsized impact on students struggling with restlessness and impulsivity.
No other ADHD-specific strategy will be effective until strong baseline classroom management is already in place.
Strong classroom management makes it possible to accurately determine which students truly need additional support or modified expectations.
Linsin suggests many students are mislabeled, over-managed, or even misdiagnosed as a result of poor classroom management rather than genuine disorder.
quotes: It's to be great at classroom management. It's to double-down on the approach we recommend here at SCM.
Because this will always have the greatest impact on students with ADHD—their improvement, contentment, and ability to focus and really enjoy school. It’s not even close.
You see, no other strategy, including those I’m going to recommend as part of a future e-guide, will have much effect until and unless the first is accomplished.
But when placed in the right environment, many will quietly assimilate into the calm and well-behaved culture just like everyone else—and without extra attention from the teacher.
There is an epidemic of students who are misunderstood, labeled, pigeonholed, over-managed, and in some cases, even misdiagnosed due to poor classroom management.
But it isn’t worth much unless you create the conditions through which all students can overcome their behavioral and academic challenges.
